cf.title: Allow pg_read_all_stats to read replication origin status

input.subject: Allow pg_read_all_stats to read replication origin status

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived against the goal or the demand. The one surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is fixable: pg_replication_origin_progress() would still deny the same LSN to the same role. The remaining choice between pg_read_all_stats and PUBLIC is a privilege-model decision, and no committer has spoken in the thread.

brief.title: Grant pg_read_all_stats read access to pg_replication_origin_status
brief.problem: Non-superusers cannot read pg_replication_origin_status, and no predefined role (pg_read_all_stats, pg_read_all_data, pg_monitor) covers it. Monitoring users who need replication origin progress must today get an explicit grant or use a superuser.
brief.proposed_design: system_views.sql grants select on the pg_replication_origin_status view and execute on its backing function pg_show_replication_origin_status() to pg_read_all_stats. Members of pg_monitor gain the same access through pg_read_all_stats. The patch adds regression tests in privileges.sql and changes no documentation.
user_visible_surface: Members of pg_read_all_stats (and so pg_monitor) can select from pg_replication_origin_status.
Members of pg_read_all_stats can execute pg_show_replication_origin_status().
author_claims: The grant follows the existing practice for monitoring views in system_views.sql.
pg_read_all_stats already covers point-in-time state views such as pg_shmem_allocations, pg_backend_memory_contexts and pg_aios, so it is not limited to cumulative statistics.
An earlier thread removed the hardcoded superuser check but stalled before granting the view to pg_read_all_stats.
Replication views use mixed access models, so a pg_read_all_stats grant is more conservative than a public grant.
brief.thread_state: Hayato Kuroda asked whether the view is statistics at all and suggested granting it to PUBLIC instead; the author argued for pg_read_all_stats. Shubhra Jain tested v2, supports the grant and leaves PUBLIC to a committer; the author's 2026-11-03 question to Kuroda has no reply.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether the pg_read_all_stats description in user-manag.sgml should change to mention the view.
The proposal does not say why a PUBLIC grant was rejected beyond the mixed precedent.
No committer has given a view on which role, or PUBLIC, should get the access.
The thread does not say whether other replication origin functions, such as pg_replication_origin_session_progress(), need a matching grant.

objections.title: Same origin progress stays superuser-only through pg_replication_origin_progress()
objections.failure_scenario: A monitoring tool running as a pg_monitor member reads remote_lsn for origin pg_16401 from pg_replication_origin_status. It then calls pg_replication_origin_progress('pg_16401', false) for the same value and gets "permission denied". The operator finds the gap only when the tool's second query fails in production.
objections.argument: After this patch, pg_replication_origin_status and pg_replication_origin_progress() expose the same per-origin LSN under different privilege rules, and the patch says nothing about the function. The brief lists this as open, and no message in the thread discusses it. A committer would likely ask for one rule for the read-only origin functions. Grants on write functions such as pg_replication_origin_advance() should stay as they are.
objections.author_must_show: Should pg_replication_origin_progress() also be granted to pg_read_all_stats, and if not, why should the same LSN need different privileges?

critic.reasoning: Execute on pg_replication_origin_progress() is revoked from public by default, and the patch grants only the view and its backing function. The thread does not discuss the function, so the same LSN would fall under two privilege rules; the question is fair and a new patch version can answer it.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: system_views.sql changes the default ACLs of pg_replication_origin_status and pg_show_replication_origin_status().

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: Members of pg_read_all_stats and pg_monitor gain read access to origin names and LSNs that are superuser-only by default today.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Should pg_replication_origin_progress() also be granted to pg_read_all_stats, and if not, why should the same LSN need different privileges?
Why is pg_read_all_stats the right holder of this access instead of PUBLIC, beyond the mixed precedent among replication views?
Does pg_replication_origin_session_progress() need a matching grant, or should it stay as it is?
Should the pg_read_all_stats description in user-manag.sgml change to mention pg_replication_origin_status?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the predefined-role privilege model and logical replication origins would have to choose between pg_read_all_stats and PUBLIC.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a default-privilege decision on one view and one function. Widening to PUBLIC later is easy, but narrowing it would break monitoring setups.
committability.author_follow_up: The author rebased the patch in message #2 and was still answering reviewers on 2026-11-03.

priority.reason: The patch adds two grants and tests in three files, and it helps monitoring users who track replication origins. It waits on a committer's choice between pg_read_all_stats and PUBLIC.

provisional_note: The code was not read, and only 3 of 8 messages were shown. The exact grant statements and what the privileges.sql tests cover could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow using replication origins in SQL level parallel sessions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a variant pg_replication_origin_session_setup(text, int) so that several SQL sessions can use the same replication origin at once. Logical replication parallel apply workers already share an origin this way, and the patch exposes that to external replication systems.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila pointed out that another thread already discusses the same feature and asked the author to give input there. The entry was then withdrawn, so the work appears to have continued in that other thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We are already discussing the same feature in an email thread [1]. Can
you check that and share your inputs there?

precedents_retrieved.title: Add more TAP coverage for archive status with crash recovery of standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Add more TAP coverage for archive status with crash recovery of standbys
Reverted commit(s): Remove some unstable parts from new TAP test for archive status check
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This part of the test was included originally in 4e87c48, but got
reverted as of f9c1b8d because of timing issues in the test, where,
after more analysis, we found that the standbys may not have recovered
from the archives all the segments needed by the test.  This stabilizes
the test by making sure that standbys replay up to the position returned
by pg_switch_wal(), meaning that all segments are recovered before the
manual checkpoint that tests WAL segment recycling and its interactions
with archive status files.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add document is_superuser
precedents_retrieved.summary: Document the is_superuser GUC in the Preset Options section of the configuration docs and move it from the UNGROUPED to the PRESET_OPTIONS group in the GUC table. The patch also removes the GUC_NO_SHOW_ALL and GUC_NO_RESET_ALL flags so that the parameter appears in SHOW ALL, and removes its separate description from the SET command docs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was reviewed and judged ready to commit, and its commit was put off to the next CommitFest because of feature freeze. Joseph Koshakow then pointed out that is_superuser is not updated when another session changes the role's superuser attribute, so it can show a stale value, and suggested that this may be why it was left undocumented. A reworded description was proposed but was disputed as also inaccurate. The visible messages do not show any further resolution before the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Perhaps this can be fixed with a show_hook? Otherwise it's probably
best not to document a GUC that can show an incorrect value.

precedents_retrieved.title: PGDOCS - inconsistent linkends to "monitoring" views
precedents_retrieved.summary: Rename a few documentation IDs and their linkends in the monitoring chapter (pg_stat_recovery_prefetch, pg_stat_subscription, pg_stat_subscription_stats) to add the "-view" suffix. This would make them match the naming used by all the other statistics views.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier asked whether renaming internal link references was worth it, since it could cause extra backpatching conflicts. John Naylor agreed the existing links were not wrong and the change was not visible to readers. No one came out in favor of the patch, so it was rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
In any case, no one has come out in favor of the patch, so it seems
like it should be rejected unless that changes.

precedents_retrieved.title: Delegating superuser tasks to new security roles
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal began as new predefined roles that let non-superusers SET and ALTER SYSTEM SET groups of superuser-only GUCs, aimed at service providers delegating control to tenants. It grew into a large patch set that also covered non-superuser event trigger owners, non-superuser subscription owners, and a narrower CREATEROLE with role-ownership hierarchies.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages show that the author split the combined patch set into four separate patch sets on new threads after several people asked for it, which ended this entry. Before the split there was unresolved disagreement. Mark Dilger noted the lack of consensus on role ownership. Stephen Frost questioned why ownership should differ from ADMIN rights and argued that event triggers should let their creator choose which roles they fire for. The visible messages do not show a specific objection that rejected the design outright.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I have now received multiple requests to split this patchset into multiple parts, including some off-list.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve monitoring of shared memory allocations
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_shmem_allocations show the full size of shared hash tables by allocating the header, directory, segments and elements in one ShmemInitStruct() call in hash_create(). It also replaces most ShmemAlloc() calls with named ShmemInitStruct() allocations so they are tracked.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The first two parts were committed and then reverted after a bug in non-shared hash tables: dir_realloc() freed a directory that was no longer allocated on its own, which caused a pfree error. Tomas Vondra did not push the fix for shared hash tables only into PG18, because dynahash is critical and its tests never run dir_realloc(). He and Amit Kapila asked for better test coverage first. The author did not add the tests, and Heikki Linnakangas later closed the entry as superseded by commit 9fe9ecd516.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This was superseded by commit 9fe9ecd516, I'll close this in the commitfest app.

precedents_retrieved.title: Orphaned users in PG16 and above can only be managed by Superusers
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Nathan Bossart, Robert Haas
precedents_retrieved.summary: Since Postgres 16, dropping role B, which created role C, leaves C with no non-superuser admin, even though B's creator A could manage C before. The patch makes DROP ROLE fail when another role would lose ADMIN privileges it inherits on a third role through the role being dropped.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected to making DROP ROLE fail because of role grants: the SQL standard says DROP ROLE revokes such grants, and the patch would make DROP ROLE fail for everyone. Nathan Bossart showed that the check depended on the order of roles in one DROP ROLE, blocked roles that had direct admin, and missed REVOKE. Robert Haas opposed the follow-up plan to add CASCADE/RESTRICT only for role grants. No new design followed, and the entry was withdrawn about a year later after Álvaro Herrera asked whether there was a plan.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: That being the case, I'm against imposing restrictions on DROP ROLE because of the properties of particular role grants.

precedents_retrieved.title: Recognizing superuser in pg_hba.conf
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add pg_hba.conf keywords "superuser" and "nonsuperuser" so entries can match on superuser status, for example to reject non-superusers from a database. A later version marked keywords with a prefix sigil such as "&" to tell them apart from role names.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers did not agree on the syntax. Tom Lane would not add more names that act as reserved words without being reserved, because an existing role name could silently change meaning in a new release. Robert Haas preferred quoting, and Stephen Frost noted that "&" can appear in role names. The thread had no further progress after January, the patch failed in the cfbot, and Daniel Gustafsson returned it with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The principle I'm concerned about is not letting a configuration file
that was perfectly fine in version N silently become a security hazard
in version N+1.

precedents_retrieved.title: Waits monitoring
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds wait-event instrumentation for heavyweight locks, LWLocks, storage I/O, network and latches, through StartWait/StopWait calls in core. A pg_stat_wait extension exposes current waits, per-backend profiles, sampled history from a background worker, and per-backend tracing to a file.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No closing message states the reason. The visible messages show overlap with a similar Robert Haas and Amit Kapila patch that adds the current wait event to pg_stat_activity, and Fujii Masao asked the author to join that discussion instead. Reviewers agreed to handle the LWLock standardization patch first, Robert Haas committed it, and the author said he would rebase his patch on it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So I think that you should attend
that discussion rather than starting new one.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums"
Reverted commit(s): Skip redundant anti-wraparound vacuums
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 2aa6e33, that added a fast path to skip
anti-wraparound and non-aggressive autovacuum jobs (these have no sense
as anti-wraparound implies aggressive).  With a cluster using a high
amount of relations with a portion of them being heavily updated, this
could cause autovacuum to lock down, with autovacuum workers attempting
repeatedly those jobs on the same relations for the same database, that
just kept being skipped.  This lock down can be solved with a manual
VACUUM FREEZE.

Justin King has reported one environment where the issue happened, and
Julien Rouhaud and I have been able to reproduce it in a second
environment.  With a very aggressive autovacuum_freeze_max_age,
triggering those jobs with pgbench is a matter of minutes, and hitting
the lock down is a lot harder (my local tests failed to do that).

Note that anti-wraparound and non-aggressive jobs can only be triggered
on a subset of shared catalogs:
- pg_auth_members
- pg_authid
- pg_database
- pg_replication_origin
- pg_shseclabel
- pg_subscription
- pg_tablespace
While the lock down was possible down to v12, the root cause of those
jobs is a much older issue, which needs more analysis.

Bonus thanks to Andres Freund for the discussion.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE"".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE"".
Reverted commit(s): Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE".
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 98fc31d6499163a0a781aa6f13582a07f09cd7c6.
That change allowed DROP OWNED BY to drop grants of the target
role to other roles, arguing that nobody would need those
privileges anymore.  But that's not so: if you're not superuser,
you still need admin privilege on the target role so you can
drop it.

It's not clear whether or how the dependency-based approach
to solving the original problem can be adapted to keep these
grants.  Since v18 release is fast approaching, the sanest
thing to do seems to be to revert this patch for now.  The
race-condition problem is low severity and not worth taking
risks for.

I didn't force a catversion bump in 98fc31d64, so I won't do
so here either.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found in the list. The thread reports an earlier discussion (messages #1, #4, #5) that removed the superuser check, then stalled before the grant; message #5 says it also proposed a PUBLIC grant. The thread records no rejection reason that would apply here.

No standards or compatibility objection to the main idea. pg_read_all_stats matches how pg_stat_replication gates LSNs, pg_dump keeps user grants through pg_init_privs, and the role choice versus PUBLIC can still be widened later. The user-manag.sgml wording is a documentation detail.

The patch only adds grants in system_views.sql, so it creates no new on-disk format, WAL record, wire message or extension API, and the catalog change is limited to ACLs on one view and one function. Standbys replay the catalog as usual, and pg_upgrade picks up the new default ACLs from initdb on the new cluster, so this angle shows no failure scenario.

The grant is read-only and goes to pg_read_all_stats, an opt-in predefined role, so default access stays superuser-only. The view shows origin names, which pg_replication_origin already exposes publicly, and LSNs, which pg_replication_slots and pg_stat_subscription already show to PUBLIC. Message #7 confirms that a monitoring role gains no table data, and the functions that modify origins stay restricted.

From the maintenance and fit angle there is nothing to object to. The patch adds two GRANT lines to system_views.sql in the same form as the existing pg_aios and pg_shmem_allocations grants, so it adds no hot-path cost, no new mechanism and no external dependency. Ten such grants per release would be acceptable, and moving the view to PUBLIC later would only widen access. The open choice between pg_read_all_stats and PUBLIC is a privilege-model question, and no committer has yet said which they prefer.

An admin can already grant select on pg_replication_origin_status and execute on pg_show_replication_origin_status() to a monitoring role, but predefined roles exist to remove those per-object grants, so that is no argument against this patch. pg_stat_subscription does not cover origins used outside built-in subscriptions, and the patch extends pg_read_all_stats instead of adding a new mechanism.

The patch adds two grants with almost no cost to non-users, and the request has come back over several years, as message #1 and messages #4 to #5 show. A plain grant works as a workaround, but asking for more demand evidence for a change this small would not hold up; the open question is which role gets the access, which another angle covers.
